target.name: AP-1 transcription factor network
target.description: AP-1 is the dimeric transcription factor built from Jun and Fos family partners, and this network describes how its rapid induction converts growth factor, cytokine and stress signals into changes in gene expression. Because FOS, FOSB, JUN and JUNB are immediate-early genes, the response is fast and self-limiting, and it sets the transcriptional tone for proliferation, differentiation, wound repair and inflammation.

target.name: protein import into mitochondrial matrix
target.description: Most mitochondrial proteins are made in the cytosol, so nearly all matrix enzymes — the citric acid cycle, fatty acid oxidation, mtDNA maintenance — depend on being escorted across two membranes after synthesis. Protein import into the mitochondrial matrix handles precursors carrying an N-terminal targeting sequence: outer-membrane receptors such as TOMM20, TOMM22 and TOMM70 recognise the signal and pass the chain through the TOMM40 channel, the TIMM23 translocase with TIMM50 and TIMM17 relays it across the inner membrane, and the presequence translocase-associated motor — TIMM44, mitochondrial Hsp70 with its cochaperones DNAJC19 and PAM16, and the nucleotide exchange factors GRPEL1/GRPEL2 — pulls it inward using the membrane potential and ATP.

target.name: epinephrine metabolic process
target.description: Epinephrine is the fight-or-flight hormone of the adrenal medulla, raising heart rate and contractility, dilating airways and mobilising glucose and fatty acids for sudden effort; the reactions that make and dispose of it are what this pathway covers. Synthesis begins with tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting step that converts tyrosine to L-DOPA and commits cells to catecholamine production, and ends with phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase, which methylates norepinephrine to epinephrine and thereby defines the adrenal chromaffin phenotype as distinct from sympathetic neurons.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on membrane traffic through the Golgi and the machinery that buds, tethers and fuses transport vesicles, the route by which secretory and lysosomal cargo reaches its destination. Its outputs are secretion, receptor recycling and delivery of hydrolases such as cathepsin D to lysosomes; when it falters, cargo is mislocalised and organelle identity degrades.

[untitled BTM module] Membrane traffic and organelle remodelling form the common thread here: newly folded cargo leaves the endoplasmic reticulum in COPII-coated vesicles built from SEC23A and SEC24B, is delivered through early endosomes marked by the tethering factor EEA1, and reaches the plasma membrane by SNARE-directed fusion, with STXBP3 acting among the Sec1/Munc18-family regulators of that step. Lipid composition and cytoskeletal geometry are managed alongside cargo flow: the inositol phosphatase SYNJ1 dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 to uncoat vesicles after endocytosis, TMEM30A serves as the accessory subunit that allows P4-ATPase flippases to translocate aminophospholipids across bilayers, and the microtubule-severing ATPase SPAST shapes tubules and axonal microtubule arrays.
